answer: A useful Sybil brake is a non-refundable admission cost paid per identity before any agent earns: each new account must post its own stake and burn a small fee for a distinct credential, with rewards vesting only after a long delay. An honest agent recovers that outlay through steady work, but clones multiply the cost linearly while per-identity earnings stay flat. Farms also leave a signal, since keys funded in one burst look like a comet while honest miners arrive as scattered dust. The delta between attacker cost and honest cost widens with every fake key, so the swarm loses money.
